subject: Stellar Labs — Dedicated GPU Pool onboarding: staging agreement & next steps
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@stellarlabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.r@stellarlabs.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool onboarding — SOW and initial questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attaching our SOW (Stellar_SOW_v1.3.pdf) and a token/QPS profile we sketched out. We're ready to move forward with a dedicated GPU pool but want to align on a few items before the kickoff: 

- Regional preference: primary in us-west-2, with failover to us-east-1.
- GPU types: prefer A100 if available, but open to A10/A30 if needed for cost.
- Autoscale/burst: we see large daily spikes (short 2–10 min bursts) that must be absorbed without degraded p99 latency. Want guidance on burst policy and pre-warming.
- KV / prefix caching: most requests reuse a small set of prompts; any cache recommendations would help reduce cost.

Can we schedule a 30-min technical handshake early next week to finalize sizing and the activation window? Diego and I are flexible on Mon/Tue morning PST.

Also, please point us to any compliance artifacts (SOC2 evidence, data retention options) we can share with our security team.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Engineering
Stellar Labs

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool onboarding — SOW and initial questions

On Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 9:12 AM Tara Singh <tara@stellarlabs.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

Hi Tara — great to see the SOW and QPS profile. Happy to jump on a short tech handshake.

Quick notes before we talk:
- Region: us-west-2 primary + us-east-1 failover is straightforward from our side; we can provision a hot-standby pool in east for fast failover or use cross-region fallback routing (tradeoff: slightly higher failover latency).
- GPUs: A100 preferred for peak p99 SLAs. We can offer mixed pools (A100 for latency-critical routes; A10 for background/cheap routes) and automatic routing by policy.
- Burst strategy: recommend a two-part approach — a small reserved headroom for instant bursts (warmed instances + prefix cache) + autoscale policy that can spin additional instances within 90–120s. We'll propose a burst credit bucket for short spikes.
- Caching: our prefix & KV caching typically reduces token compute by 20–40% for reuse patterns. We'll need sample request traces (anonymized) to tune cache TTLs.

Next steps:
1) Can we book Tue Apr 6, 10:00 AM PST for 30 min? I'll invite Monica (implementation PM) and Rishi (inference eng).
2) I'll share a short pre-kickoff worksheet (small form) to capture expected QPS by route, model choices, and SLA targets.

Thanks — looking forward.

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara@stellarlabs.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.r@stellarlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool onboarding — technical handshake notes

Thanks all for the quick call. Notes + follow-ups from our side: 

Call recap (30m):
- Workloads: 3 routes (embed, chat-bot, customer-facing summarization). Peak combined concurrent requests ~220 qps for 2–3 mins daily; baseline ~35 qps. Token mix attached in their CSV.
- Models: they plan to start with an open LLM v1.3 (decoder) and add a quantized lower-cost variant for background jobs.

Technical recommendations (preliminary):
1) Pool sizing: start with 8 A100s (pinned to 40 concurrent model workers each), plus 4 A10s for background fallback. This gives us a buffer for p99 headroom while keeping cost predictable.
2) Autoscale policy:
   - Base reserved capacity: 8 A100 equivalents (always-on).
   - Burst pool: allow additional up to 6 A100 equiv to spin up (120s target) with pre-warm window of 2 instances kept ready.
   - Use a short token-based alarm to trigger burst when 95th percentile token backlog > threshold for 30s.
3) Caching: enable prefix cache with 30–90s TTL; recommend a small KV shard per GPU node. We'll sample traces to set TTL.
4) Routing: set critical routes (chat-bot) to prefer A100; non-critical to use A10 fallback. Canary during rollout for 10% traffic.

Questions for Stellar: 
- Can you share a scrubbed sample of 2 hours of request logs (timestamps + route + token length + model id)? We need that to finalize TTLs and concurrency.
- Any regulatory constraints on cross-region traffic?

I'll draft a short activation runbook (steps, owners, rollback) and share by EOD.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

--- Attachment referenced: estimated_qps_and_token_profile.csv

From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@stellarlabs.com>

Date: Thu, 07 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool onboarding — technical handshake notes

Logan / Rishi — thanks for the recommendations. A few quick answers: 

- We'll provide a 2-hour anonymized trace by end of day today (removing PII).
- No hard prohibition on cross-region traffic but prefer encryption in transit and audit logs visible to us.
- GPU preference: we'd like to try mixed pool as you suggested; cost is a factor so please include a monthly estimate for both the 8A100+4A10 and a lower-cost 4A100+8A10 variant.

Two asks before the activation window: 
1) Security package: can you send the SOC2 summary and typical audit artifacts (we don't need raw reports, a checklist is fine)?
2) Runbook: we need an ops-friendly runbook we can share with our on-call. Rishi — will review your draft.

We propose a soft activation (internal traffic only) the week of Apr 18 and full cutover Apr 25, pending confirmation.

Thanks,
Diego Ramos
Engineering Manager, Platform
Stellar Labs

Date: Thu, 07 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool onboarding — staging agreement & owners (next steps)

Hi Tara / Diego — thanks for the quick turnaround and the trace. From our side we pulled together an initial staging agreement and owner matrix below. This is a short operational agreement meant to keep the activation low-risk. Please reply with any changes; otherwise we'll treat this as accepted and begin provisioning on Apr 11.

Staging agreement (summary)
- Staging window: Apr 18–21 (internal traffic only).
- Full cutover: Apr 25 (target; final date locked by Apr 20).
- Regions: us-west-2 primary; us-east-1 failover (hot-standby).
- Pool proposal: 8x A100 + 4x A10 (option B: 4x A100 + 8x A10 for cost-saving).
- Autoscale: reserved baseline 8 A100 equiv; burst to +6 A100 equiv (120s spin-up target). Pre-warm 2 instances during predicted peak windows.
- Canary: 10% traffic to new pool for the first 48h, automatic rollback if p99 > SLA for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.

Owners & tickets
- Redwood infra lead (provisioning & pool creation): Karthik Iyer — ticket #INF-7842
- Activation runbook & rollback plan: Rishi Malhotra — ticket #INF-7843
- Customer-side verification & cutover decision: Tara Singh / Diego Ramos — ticket #STEL-2219
- Compliance artifacts & access: Logan Wright — ticket #SEC-1120 (I'll share SOC2 checklist link once cleared for distribution)

Requested deliverables this week
- Redwood: activation runbook draft (Rishi) + provisioning ETA (Karthik) by Apr 9.
- Stellar: anonymized 2-hour trace + confirmation on GPU-cost option by Apr 9.

If all good, we'll provision the base pool on Apr 11 and share access to the staging endpoint by Apr 15.

Monica Patel
